mechanism_name: AOSP overlayfs remount shadowing (fs_mgr_overlayfs / adb remount scratch)
how_it_works: AOSP's fs_mgr contains a generic feature (fs_mgr_overlayfs, documented in system/core/fs_mgr/README.overlayfs.md) that lets a userdebug/eng-style build make a read-only-by-fstab partition (typically /system) appear writable without touching the underlying block device. When engaged, the kernel mounts an overlayfs whose lowerdir is the real partition and whose upperdir/workdir live on a separate writable backing store; any file that exists in the upper layer always wins over the same path in the lower layer, and once an upper copy of a file exists it is never re-read from the lower layer again. Per the AOSP README, this backing store is '/cache/overlay/' for non-A/B devices, or '/mnt/scratch/overlay' (a dynamic 'scratch' partition carved out of super, or the alternate system_ slot) for A/B/LRAP devices -- the README explicitly states the AOSP team made an architectural decision to NOT use /data/overlay for this. The scratch/overlay mechanism is normally engaged by `adb disable-verity && adb remount`, but a device can also ship from the factory with it pre-provisioned if the OEM's build/recovery tooling invoked the same fs_mgr code path (e.g. during OEM development or an OTA/rescue flow) -- overlayfs setup does not require AVB to be enforcing; it only needs CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS=y in the kernel and the fstab entry(ies) to be eligible for overlay, which is independent of vbmeta's verification flag. [uncertain] Critically for the timing symptom observed here: per the AOSP first-stage init source (init/first_stage_mount.cpp), the overlay is assembled in first-stage init -- specifically fs_mgr_mount_overlayfs_fstab_entry() and MapScratchPartitionIfNeeded()/fs_mgr_overlayfs_mount_all() run right after TrySwitchSystemAsRoot()/switch_root and strictly BEFORE init re-execs into second-stage init and parses any init.rc. This means that on a genuine full boot, whatever upper-layer content was captured at the time the overlay/scratch was first created is what gets merged over the freshly-edited /system before init.rc is ever read -- so an edit made directly to the raw partition (bypassing fs_mgr) is structurally invisible to the booted OS regardless of how correct the raw write was.
fits_observed_symptoms: (1) Write succeeds and is visible pre-reboot -- FITS: the recovery-side loop-mount reads/writes the raw ext4 lower layer directly; no overlay is assembled in recovery (recovery boots a separate ramdisk/image and does not run the same first-stage fs_mgr overlay logic against the normal boot fstab), so the edit is exactly what recovery sees. (2) Survives unmount/remount within the same recovery session -- FITS: re-mounting the same raw block device in recovery just re-reads the same lower-layer bytes; no overlay recombination happens in recovery, so nothing can 're-shadow' it mid-session. (3) Reverts only after a real power-cycle boot -- FITS WELL and is the most discriminating symptom: only a genuine boot invokes first-stage init's MountPartitions()/switch_root()/fs_mgr_mount_overlayfs_fstab_entry()/fs_mgr_overlayfs_mount_all() sequence that reconstructs upper(stale)+lower(edited) into the merged view second-stage init and init.rc actually see. (4) boot_completed marker addition to init.rc never appears in /cache -- FITS: if the merged/effective init.rc is the stale upper copy (lacking the added trigger), the trigger+service simply never exists at runtime, so no marker is ever written, independent of whether /cache is itself also serving as the overlay's backing store. (5) AVB/vbmeta already fully disabled -- COMPATIBLE, does not rule this out: fs_mgr_overlayfs engagement is gated by build/debuggability and an explicit disable-verity/remount state, not by AVB signature validity; an unenforced, unsigned vbmeta (flags=2, algorithm_type=0) has no bearing on whether an overlay was previously provisioned. (6) /system is ext4, not squashfs -- COMPATIBLE, does not rule this out: fs_mgr_overlayfs applies to any fstab-managed partition eligible for overlay, most commonly ext4/f2fs; squashfs is not a prerequisite (squashfs devices use it because they have no other way to become writable at all, but ext4 devices can still be overlaid instead of remounted directly if a scratch/overlay was already set up). (7) Non-A/B device -- COMPATIBLE with a nuance [uncertain]: the AOSP default backing store for non-A/B is /cache/overlay/, not a super-embedded 'scratch' logical partition; however if this device has no dedicated physical /cache by-name partition (not confirmed in the given partition facts), fs_mgr's scratch-in-super mechanism (dynamic partition named 'scratch', mapped via device-mapper) is used instead regardless of A/B-ness, which would also explain why liblp reports metadata_slot_count=2 even though by-name shows no A/B slots -- that field alone is inconclusive and needs direct inspection.
known_precedent: The mechanism itself is officially documented generic AOSP behavior (system/core/fs_mgr/README.overlayfs.md), not vendor- or device-specific code, so it ships unmodified in effectively every AOSP-derived build unless a vendor explicitly strips CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS or the fs_mgr overlay hooks. No Rockchip RK3326-specific or 'TXCZ'/Android-Go-STB-specific writeup describing this exact symptom was found. [uncertain] The closest concrete precedent found is a TI Sitara AM625 (embedded/STB-class SoC, similar deployment profile to this projector box) forum thread on remounting /system read-write on Android, which runs into the same fs_mgr overlay/scratch behavior, plus the existence of community 'magisk_overlayfs' modules whose entire purpose is to manually stand up this exact overlay to get a writable /system on production devices -- both confirm this is a widely-encountered, well-understood class of behavior on embedded Android devices generally, even without an RK3326-specific report.
likelihood: High -- it is the only mechanism among the classic candidates (AVB, dm-verity, SELinux, a live service undoing the edit) that (a) is not already ruled out by the given device facts and (b) independently predicts the single most specific and hardest-to-fake symptom: reverting only on a full boot, before init.rc is parsed, while surviving arbitrary remounts within the same recovery session.
test_procedure:
All commands below assume the existing recovery root shell (adb root already works there). Do the raw/offline checks first, then boot normally and use adb to check the live system.

A. Check for a dynamic 'scratch' partition inside super (from recovery, read-only, safe):
   ls -la /dev/block/by-name/ | grep -i -E 'cache|scratch'
   lpdump /dev/block/by-name/super          # or lpdump --slot=0 super if it needs a slot arg
   # If lpdump is not present in this recovery image, fall back to a raw string scan (read-only):
   strings /dev/block/by-name/super | grep -i scratch

B. If a physical cache partition exists, mount it read-only and look for the AOSP overlay layout (<mountpoint>/overlay/<partition>/{upper,work}):
   mkdir -p /mnt/cache_ro
   mount -t ext4 -o ro /dev/block/by-name/cache /mnt/cache_ro   # try f2fs if ext4 fails
   ls -la /mnt/cache_ro/overlay/ 2>/dev/null
   ls -la /mnt/cache_ro/overlay/system/ 2>/dev/null
   umount /mnt/cache_ro

C. Plant a unique canary in the raw partition before rebooting, so you can tell later whether the booted system read the raw partition or a stale upper:
   echo '# CANARY_$(date +%s)' >> /path/to/mounted/system/etc/init/hw/init.rc   # adjust to wherever init.rc actually lives on this SAR layout
   sync

D. Reboot normally (power-cycle, not just recovery unmount/remount), then from a host with adb:
   adb wait-for-device
   adb root && adb wait-for-device
   adb shell cat /proc/mounts | grep -E 'overlay| / | /system '
   adb shell mount | grep -i overlay
   adb shell ls -la /dev/block/mapper/ | grep -i scratch
   adb shell cat /system/etc/init/hw/init.rc | grep CANARY   # expect: NOT found, confirming shadowing
   adb shell getprop | grep -i verity

   Interpretation: if /proc/mounts shows a line with fs type 'overlay' and lowerdir=/system (or lowerdir=/ for a root overlay) plus an upperdir= pointing at /cache/overlay/... or /mnt/scratch/overlay/..., the mechanism is CONFIRMED. If /system instead mounts directly as ext4 straight off the dm-linear/system block device with no overlay entry at all, this mechanism is RULED OUT and the revert has some other cause.

E. Cross-check by writing post-boot and looking for it on the raw partition back in recovery:
   adb shell 'echo POSTBOOT_MARK >> /system/etc/init/hw/init.rc'
   adb reboot recovery
   # back in recovery, without going through fs_mgr:
   grep -a POSTBOOT_MARK /path/to/loop-mounted/raw/system/etc/init/hw/init.rc
   # If POSTBOOT_MARK is NOT found on the raw partition, post-boot writes are landing in an overlay upper elsewhere -- strong independent confirmation.
bypass_or_fix:
Once confirmed, the goal is to remove/neutralize the stale upper layer (or stop overlay engagement entirely) so writes to the raw partition, or the normal remount flow, actually take effect on boot.

1. AOSP-blessed path (try first, cheap, but may no-op since AVB is already unsigned/unenforced):
   adb enable-verity
   adb reboot
   # README.overlayfs.md documents this as freeing OverlayFS and reverting the device to the pre-override state.

2. Manual/direct path (use if step 1 has no effect, which is likely given vbmeta algorithm_type=0/unsigned): clear the overlay's upper/work contents without touching the super partition table or any signing/verity metadata:
   - If backing store is the super-embedded 'scratch' partition found in step A: locate its device-mapper node once mapped (adb shell ls /dev/block/mapper/scratch, or from recovery if fs_mgr already mapped it), mount it read-write, and remove only the overlay content directories:
       mount -t ext4 -o rw /dev/block/mapper/scratch /mnt/scratch_rw
       rm -rf /mnt/scratch_rw/overlay/system
       umount /mnt/scratch_rw
   - If backing store is /cache/overlay/ (physical cache partition, non-A/B default):
       mount -t ext4 -o rw /dev/block/by-name/cache /mnt/cache_rw
       rm -rf /mnt/cache_rw/overlay
       umount /mnt/cache_rw
   Do NOT delete or resize the scratch logical partition entry itself via liblp/lpmake -- clearing its file contents is sufficient and far safer than editing super's partition metadata.

3. Redo the intended edit directly on the raw /system partition (as before), power-cycle reboot, then re-run the detection commands from test_procedure step D to confirm /proc/mounts no longer shows an 'overlay' entry for /system (or, if a fresh empty overlay gets recreated, that it now passes the edited lower content through since its upper is empty).

4. Going forward, avoid running `adb remount` / `adb disable-verity` again on this device unless you intend to go back to overlay-based editing -- doing so re-provisions a fresh scratch/overlay and will resume shadowing any future direct raw-partition edits.
risk_level: Detection steps (A, B, D, E) are read-only or write only to a scratch/temp mount point and are fully safe/reversible. The fix in step 1 (adb enable-verity) is low risk and standard AOSP tooling. The fix in step 2 is a targeted content deletion (not a partition-table edit) and is low-to-moderate risk: it only removes overlay upper/work directories, is reversible by re-running adb remount if something is wrong, and deliberately avoids touching liblp/super metadata to prevent a boot-affecting mistake. Do not attempt to remove the scratch logical partition entry from super's metadata directly -- that step carries real risk of corrupting the dynamic-partition table and should be avoided in favor of the content-clearing approach above.
